purpose: Floors and a ceiling for the page-level color-energy check (scripts/validate_page_color.py), derived from the two owner-supplied Go Full Page reference pages, VA and VB. They are the only calibration inputs; no output of any run was used to set a number.

derivation.rule: band = max(|VA - VB|, tolerance). Floor = min(VA, VB) - band. Ceiling = max(VA, VB) + band.
derivation.tolerance: 10 percent of the weaker reference for the 0-1 metrics (resampling and crop noise; the half-scale and quarter-scale scripts of the analysis differed by 0.2 points on a 15 percent figure); 8 levels of 255 for black_point and white_point (JPEG and resampling noise at a clean black or white).
derivation.why_floors_not_targets: VA and VB are two valid examples of one system, not a spec. Their spread is the measured room between two good pages, so a page is allowed to be as weak as the weaker reference minus that spread, never weaker. A page between the references passes; a page below both fails.
derivation.hero_hue_floor: Derived the same way from the share of pixels that are saturated and within 15 degrees of each reference's own red (VA #BF031C, VB #B80000). It is evaluated only when the client's hero hex is passed (--hero), and it is the one metric that depends on the client's palette. The analysis measured the same family at 25.6 percent (VA) and 18.3 percent (VB) with a hue-angle test; the 0.5 point difference is the resampling method.

notes: A PAGE check. Run it on a stitched page or a full render. One section slice is mostly one ground and is not meaningful.

Desktop calibration. VA and VB are desktop captures. A mobile stitch is measured the same way, but no mobile reference exists; treat a mobile result as informational until a mobile reference is supplied.

near_black_share counts V < 0.20 so a brand dark such as navy or deep green counts. A client whose darkest palette color has V of 0.25 or more has no dark ground to measure and needs an owner ruling, not a lower threshold.
near_white_share and white_point cannot tell a client's own cream from white: a client light color is on-role by definition. They prove a clean light ground exists, nothing about its hue.

Not measured here, reviewer-judged traits: ground order and longest same-ground run, off-role light grounds, divider bands, accent panels. Reference implementations are in the SPF020 analysis tools (hue_split.py, ground_pastel.py).
